issues.detail: Code samples ignore error handling (no res.ok check, GraphQL errors not inspected, no handling of rate limits/429 or failed POST responses), and edge cases like pagination beyond the first page are not covered.

scenarios.name: headless-newest-products-graphql
scenarios.rationale: B queries `site.products(first: $first, sortBy: NEWEST)` against the `/graphql` endpoint with a Bearer token from an env var, selects the expected fields and notes the 50-per-page limit with first: 8, which matches the rubric. A uses a `newestProducts` connection and never adds `sortBy: NEWEST` inside `products(...)`, and it doesn't mention the 50-per-page limit.

scenarios.name: create-product-and-list-awaiting-orders
scenarios.rationale: Both meet every rubric item (POST to /v3/catalog/products with X-Auth-Token, physical type, price and weight, V2 /v2/orders with status_id=11, and a server-side env token); B is slightly better because it handles 204 responses inside a helper, adds a try/catch, and doesn't invent a placeholder category ID like A's categories: [23] that would fail.

scenarios.name: scaffold-catalyst-storefront
scenarios.rationale: B gives all three required commands, Node.js 24 and pnpm prerequisites, the store hash/channel prompts and .env.local, and warns against the old Vercel commerce template; A hedges on the Node version (20/22), uses `npm create` instead of `pnpm create`, omits the Vercel warning, and says `pnpm dev` rather than `pnpm run dev`.
